uncited: It builds on [Near-Surface Point Sampling](2910-near-surface-point-sampling.md) by using distance-field estimation to restrict particle placement to a specific band around the isosurface.
*   A 3D vector field $V(x,y,z)$ defined on a rectilinear lattice.
*   A scalar function $f(x,y,z)$ defined on the same rectilinear lattice.
*   A contour value $C$ defining the surface $f(x,y,z) = C$.
*   A distance parameter $D$ defining the thickness of the region around the contour.
*   A particle count $N$ per marked cell.
*   A rendered image containing semi-transparent, motion-blurred ellipsoidal particles overlaid on the contour surface.
**Lattice Grid:** Stores values for $f(x,y,z)$ and the precomputed magnitude of its gradient $|\nabla f(x,y,z)|$ at each vertex.
*   $|\nabla f|$ is computed via finite differences of neighboring vertex values of $f$.
**Cell Marking Array:** A boolean flag for each lattice cell indicating if it intersects the region $d(x,y,z) < D$.
*   A cell is marked if at least one of its vertices is within distance $D$ of the contour surface.
**Particle Linked List:** Stores active particles.
For each lattice vertex, approximate the gradient $\nabla f$ using finite differences of neighboring vertex values of $f$.
*   Identify all lattice vertices within distance $D$ of the contour surface $f(x,y,z)=C$.
*   Mark all lattice cells that have at least one marked vertex.
*   For each marked cell, randomly insert $N$ particles within the cell boundaries.
*   Check that all marked cells still contain $N$ particles.
*   Render the opaque contour surface first.
Trilinearly interpolate the scalar value $f(x,y,z)$ from the eight surrounding lattice vertices.
Trilinearly interpolate the gradient magnitude $|\nabla f(x,y,z)|$ from the eight surrounding lattice vertices.
Particles are drawn as blurred ellipses stretched in the direction of motion.
A single blurred disk texture is mapped to a 3D rectangle defined by four vertices.
